result.process_description:
The sales clerks in a bank can use their software frontend to receive the credit-scoring for a certain customer. 
This starts a process in the banking system which communicates with the agency in the background. 
This process sends a scoring request to the agency right after the beginning. 
Then, the Agency does a first quick scoring (level 1). 
This will often lead to an immediate result which is then returned directly to the banking system within seconds. 
The banking process presents the result to the clerk sitting at the frontend. 
Sometimes the scoring cannot be determined immediately and takes longer. 
In this case the agency informs the banking process of the delay and then starts the level 2 scoring (which can take up to a couple of minutes). 
After the scoring result is determined, the information is sent back to the banking process. 
The banking process displays a message to the clerk when he receives information about the delay to check again later. 
As soon as the result arrives, it can be seen at the frontend.

result.rule: Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.
Verify processRef values, lane membership, message-flow endpoints and directions, and the prohibition on sequence flows between pools.

result.rule: When the description says an external participant performs a computation or evaluation step (such as a calculation or assessment) before it replies, and the process sends that participant a request and receives replies or notices back from it: Model the external participant's computation step as a task inside that participant's pool, not as an intermediate catch event in the process pool. Model each request sent to the participant as a message flow from the process pool to the participant's pool, and each reply or notice the participant returns as a message flow from its pool back to the process. Where the description gives alternative paths (for example an immediate reply versus a delayed one), make that decision with an exclusive gateway in the process pool. Use an intermediate catch event in the process only where the process itself is described as waiting for a message, signal, time or condition.

When the description is written in the first person by a role that performs the case work itself, and that role's own steps send requests to an external party and then depend on that party's replies, payments or objections to choose the next step: Model the performing role as its own participant pool that holds its tasks, gateways and events. Model the external party as a separate participant pool. Connect the two pools with message flows for each request the performing role sends and each reply, payment or objection the external party returns. Do not merge the external party's actions into the performing role's pool or lane.

When the description has an interactive software system, used by a person in one participant's organization, that sends a request to a process run by another participant and must receive that process's outcome back in the system: Model the software system as its own black-box pool with no internal workflow. Connect its request to a message start event in the other participant's process pool with a message flow. Connect that process's final send task back to the same software system pool with a message flow. Do not represent this exchange as a sequence flow, and do not fold the software system into a lane of the other pool or replace it with a generic person pool.

When the description says one participant asks several outside parties to return a response and then picks one of those responses, and gives no steps for the outside parties beyond returning their response: Model the request and the selection as tasks in the lane of the requesting participant, in the order the description states them, with a gateway only if the outcome branches. Do not create a separate pool for the outside parties and do not add message flows to or from them. Use a separate pool with message flows only when the description gives the outside parties their own steps or treats them as independent communicating participants.
